summary: This is an early-stage game called "space mission", and as a solo developer with limited resources, I couldn't polish every single detail to perfection. In real life, I'm an engineer who loves operating all kinds of machinery. When I was a kid, a manga about NASA astronaut selection deeply inspired me. Operating a robotic arm in space for precision docking and assisting astronauts with extravehicular movements is far more complex than on Earth. Through this game, I hope to offer a realistic yet accessible way for kids to understand what it's truly like to be a space station robotic arm operator.
details:
Multi-Camera & Spatial Control: Players must monitor multiple camera feeds to navigate orientation, controlling both the translation and rotation of the robotic arm while coordinating with Mission Control and ISS astronauts.

AI-Generated Scenarios: Mission environments and events are procedurally generated by AI based on real-world spaceflight incidents.

LLM-Powered Communications: Dialogue interactions can leverage existing Large Language Models (LLMs) for roleplay, with the potential to fine-tune on additional NASA and partner agency datasets for heightened realism.
